item.title: Gate One configuration
item.description:
Generated from schemas/api-routes.schema.json by scripts/gen-config-docs. Do not edit this page: edit the schema or the generator.

The api-routes.json file consumed by the gate-one binary. Relative paths (certificates, keys, plugin artefacts, WAL directories) are resolved from the configuration file.

Fields

Field Type Required Description

securityHeaders

object

no

Platform-wide response hardening, emitted by the gateway on EVERY response it serves (proxied or generated: health, stats, 401/403, MCP metadata, PWA assets, CSP collector). Declaring the block applies the secure defaults; each field can be tightened or disabled. Referrer-Policy is only set when the response does not already carry one (a proxified app’s stricter policy wins). Absent = nothing (an install whose edge proxy already sets them can opt out).

license

object

no

Optional offline signed licence (Ed25519). Absent, invalid or expired = evaluation/personal mode: the gateway keeps serving; the user badge shows a notice. The private signing key NEVER ships (only publicKey is embedded).

authProvider

object

no

Authentication provider. dev is the embedded loopback-only IdP used for onboarding/tests; http-bridge is any external service implementing the Gate One HTTP bridge contract (auth-bridge is the reference implementation; a non-conforming service needs an adapter); oidc is the native Relying Party (discovery, code+PKCE, JWKS, session, logout, MCP resource server); jwt is a stateless bearer verifier. Absent = legacy oidc + auth-bridge translation, so existing configs are unchanged. The legacy type http is accepted as a deprecated alias of http-bridge.

authProviders

array of object

no

Named authentication providers for per-route binding. Mutually exclusive with the legacy singular authProvider. Each item uses the same fields as authProvider plus id/cookieName; a route selects one with auth.provider.

defaultAuthProvider

string

no

Provider id used by routes that do not set auth.provider. Required when more than one authProviders entry is declared.

defaultAppUrl

string

no

Global fallback for a bare visit to a login host root (302), preserving the query string. A provider’s own defaultAppUrl wins for its login host. Email verification/account links must carry a return target; use defaultAppUrl only as an operational fallback.

oidc

object

no

LEGACY platform IdP block. When authProvider is absent, it is translated into an http provider (auth-bridge) at load; existing configs keep working. New configurations should use authProvider.

tokenBroker

object

no

Internal per-user credential broker. Required only when a route declares upstream.delegated. The shared secret is read from the named environment variable at load (never from this file) and is never logged.

mcpDefaults

object

no

Optional defaults shared by every MCP access unit.

mcpSets

object

no

Named groups of MCP services exposed with their own access rights (resource/scope/identity) and per-member tool filters. A member endpoint is set.host + set.endpoint + member.path.

usage

object

no

Out-of-process usage-event bus (WAL + extension plugins). Presence enables it. Events are produced only for the subscribed types; a full durable share is answered with a targeted 503 (health/readyz/auth-probe exempt).

routes

array of object

yes

Routes served by this gateway. Order is not significant: the most specific host/path match wins.

ssoGroups

array of object

no

Cross-domain SSO groups. Shared OIDC/client/session settings are declared once per group; providers[] declares only what varies per application domain. Expanded into authProviders at load. Auth-registry is exhaustive: a shared field placed in a provider entry is rejected by the strict decoder.

securityHeaders

Platform-wide response hardening, emitted by the gateway on EVERY response it serves (proxied or generated: health, stats, 401/403, MCP metadata, PWA assets, CSP collector). Declaring the block applies the secure defaults; each field can be tightened or disabled. Referrer-Policy is only set when the response does not already carry one (a proxified app’s stricter policy wins). Absent = nothing (an install whose edge proxy already sets them can opt out).

Field Type Required Description

hstsMaxAge

integer

no

Strict-Transport-Security max-age, in seconds. Absent = 15552000 (180 days); 0 = header omitted (e.g. a host that must stay reachable in plain HTTP). Keep includeSubDomains/preload off until every subdomain is HTTPS-only: with preload the choice becomes permanent in browsers. Minimum: 0. Maximum: 63072000.

hstsIncludeSubDomains

boolean

no

Append includeSubDomains. Default false.

hstsPreload

boolean

no

Append preload. Requires hstsIncludeSubDomains (refused at load otherwise). Default false.

nosniff

boolean

no

X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Default true.

referrerPolicy

string (one of: `, `no-referrer, no-referrer-when-downgrade, origin, origin-when-cross-origin, same-origin, strict-origin, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, unsafe-url)

no

Referrer-Policy value. Absent = strict-origin-when-cross-origin; empty string = header omitted.

license

Optional offline signed licence (Ed25519). Absent, invalid or expired = evaluation/personal mode: the gateway keeps serving; the user badge shows a notice. The private signing key NEVER ships (only publicKey is embedded).

Field Type Required Description

token

string

no

Signed licence token: v1.<base64url(JSON claims)>.<base64url(signature)>.

tokenFile

string

no

Path to a file holding the token (mounted secret, easy renewal: replace the file + SIGHUP). Overridden by GATE_ONE_LICENSE_TOKEN; falls back to token when unreadable.

publicKey

string

no

Ed25519 public key, base64 (raw 32 bytes). Public by design, safe to commit. Legacy single-key form (tokens without kid).

publicKeys

object

no

kid → Ed25519 public key (base64). Several keys can be valid at once during a rotation; tokens carry their signed kid. An unknown kid is rejected.

url

string

no

Registration/pricing URL shown by the badge.

authProvider

Authentication provider. dev is the embedded loopback-only IdP used for onboarding/tests; http-bridge is any external service implementing the Gate One HTTP bridge contract (auth-bridge is the reference implementation; a non-conforming service needs an adapter); oidc is the native Relying Party (discovery, code+PKCE, JWKS, session, logout, MCP resource server); jwt is a stateless bearer verifier. Absent = legacy oidc + auth-bridge translation, so existing configs are unchanged. The legacy type http is accepted as a deprecated alias of http-bridge.

Field Type Required Description

type

string (one of: dev, http-bridge, http, oidc, jwt)

no

Provider implementation. Default: dev when a dev block is present, oidc when clientId is present, jwt when jwksUrl is present, http-bridge otherwise. http is a deprecated alias of http-bridge.

id

string

no

Unique provider id when declared in authProviders. The legacy authProvider block is normalized to id "default".

cookieName

string

no

Session cookie name for type oidc. Empty = gate_one_session for the default provider, a provider-scoped name for additional providers.

baseUrl

string

no

Service root for type http-bridge (default http://auth-bridge:3000, or AUTH_BRIDGE_URL).

loginBaseUrl

string

no

Public origin of the login service. For dev it hosts the embedded login page, e.g. http://login.demo.localhost:3000 (no path/query).

loginUrl

string

no

Full login page URL. Defaults to loginBaseUrl + /login, then (type http-bridge) the legacy oidc.loginUrl, then baseUrl + /login.

issuer

string

no

OIDC issuer advertised in MCP protected-resource metadata. Defaults to the legacy oidc.issuer, or loginBaseUrl + /dev for dev.

cookieDomain

string

no

Shared parent domain of the session cookie (dev), e.g. demo.localhost. Required for dev.

defaultAppUrl

string

no

Application to send a bare visit to THIS provider’s login host root to. Overrides the global defaultAppUrl for this login host. Must be a route host bound to this provider or a host covered by its cookieDomain.

verifyUrl

string

no

Identity verification endpoint (type http-bridge). Default baseUrl + /auth.

mcpVerifyUrl

string

no

MCP bearer verification endpoint (type http-bridge). Default baseUrl + /auth/mcp.

healthUrl

string

no

Readiness endpoint (type http-bridge). Default baseUrl + /health.

headers

object

no

Maps the identity response headers of an external provider (type http-bridge). Empty = auth-bridge defaults.

clientId

string

no

OIDC client ID (type oidc). The client must be registered at the IdP with the redirect URI below.

clientSecretEnv

string

no

Environment variable holding the OIDC client secret (type oidc). Absent/empty = public client (PKCE only). Never put the secret in this file.

scopes

array of string

no

OIDC scopes requested at the authorization endpoint. Default: openid, profile, email.

redirectUrl

string

no

OIDC callback URL registered at the IdP. Default: loginBaseUrl + /auth/callback.

roleClaims

array of string

no

Dot paths in the ID token whose values become roles (default: realm_access.roles, resource_access.<clientId>.roles, groups).

scopesClaim

string

no

Claim holding the granted scopes (default scope; scp is always also read).

mcpAudience

string

no

MCP access-token audience policy. Empty = scope-only (compatible default). A literal value requires that value in aud. "auto" requires the endpoint’s own protected-resource identifier (recommended, and used with Keycloak audience mappers).

jwksUrl

string

no

JWKS endpoint for type jwt. Required for jwt; the provider never hosts a login page.

audience

string

no

Expected audience for type jwt (empty = no audience check, or the MCP resource when VerifyMCP is used).

algorithms

array of string

no

Accepted JWT signing algorithms. Default: the algorithms advertised by the JWKS/issuer.

header

string

no

Bearer header name for type jwt. Default Authorization.

cacheTtlSeconds

integer

no

JWKS cache TTL for type jwt. Default 300. Minimum: 0.

sessionTtlSeconds

integer

no

OIDC RP session lifetime. Default 3600 (1h): a short TTL bounds revocation when no shared store is used. The refresh/reauth flow renews it. Minimum: 1.

links

object

no

Links owned by the authentication connector, displayed in the user badge. account is the IdP’s own account console: NO OIDC standard, so the URL is explicit (Keycloak /realms/<realm>/account/, Entra myaccount.microsoft.com, Google myaccount.google.com, Okta /enduser/settings…).

sessionKeyEnv

string

no

Environment variable holding the RP cookie signing key (base64/random string, hashed to 32 bytes). Empty = the key is generated and persisted in the bbolt store. Required for multi-instance (shared key).

sessionStore

object

no

RP-side revocation store (back-channel logout, RP logout). Default: bbolt at ./gate-one-state.db, relative to the config file. bbolt is single-writer: a second Gate One instance on the same file is refused. Redis is the shared, multi-instance backend and makes revocation visible on the next request on every instance.

backchannelLogout

boolean

no

OIDC Back-Channel Logout. Absent = auto: enabled when the IdP discovery advertises backchannel_logout_supported. false disables it. Register <loginBaseUrl>/backchannel-logout at the IdP.

legacyTokenCookies

boolean

no

Migration bridge: also set auth-bridge’s access_token/refresh_token/id_token cookies on cookieDomain, so auth-bridge’s token-broker proxy routes (/connections, /connect, /oauth) resolve the same session when both share the login host. Default false. The native session cookie remains authoritative for Gate One.

backchannelForwardUrl

string

no

Migration bridge: after a valid local back-channel revocation, POST the same logout_token to this auth-bridge /backchannel-logout URL so its persistent sid list stays in sync for /auth and /connections. Best effort.

revocationTtlSeconds

integer

no

Retention of revocation entries. Default: the issuer’s advertised refresh-token TTL (cladone_refresh_token_ttl_seconds, e.g. the broker), else 30 days; never shorter than the session TTL. Must cover the refresh-token lifetime for a global logout. Minimum: 1.

dev

object

no

Embedded development IdP. Loopback-only; never production.

Maps the identity response headers of an external provider (type http-bridge). Empty = auth-bridge defaults.

routes

Field Type Required Description

host

string

no

Single literal application host (or wildcard pattern when wildcard is set). Mutually exclusive with hosts.

hosts

array of string

no

Literal application hosts sharing this route body. Expanded at load into one concrete route per host; auth.provider is inferred from the ssoGroups provider whose cookieDomain covers each host. Mutually exclusive with host and wildcard.

wildcard

object

no

Named host/backend expansion — one route, N sites. Keys = capture names ({name} in host and backend), values = the ALLOW-LISTS of DNS labels they may take (a-z0-9, hyphens, no dots). The route expands at load into one concrete route per label; a label outside the lists has no route (fail-closed: the backend is never attacker-derived). With rewriteBody enabled, the expansion also compiles the cross-route map: an origin of another variant (e.g. es.wikipedia.org in the English edition) is rewritten to that sibling’s public host; ambiguous alias mappings are left alone, and route-local except prefixes do not apply to siblings.

path

string

yes

Prefix; "/*" = wildcard (whole host).

stripPrefix

string

no

Exact PUBLIC path prefix removed from the request before it reaches the backend. Path only (no query, fragment or wildcard), matched on segment boundaries and normalized at load (trailing slash removed; root "/" forbidden). Example: path "/api/*", stripPrefix "/api", backend "http://api:8080/v1" turns /api/foo into /v1/foo. The backend also receives X-Forwarded-Prefix when the ingress did not set one. Response paths are rewritten symmetrically: Location, Content-Location, Refresh/Link headers, Set-Cookie Path, and HTML URL attributes (href/src/action/srcset/poster, style url(), meta refresh) are brought back under /api; relative references and other origins are left untouched. Script strings and CSS @import are out of scope. Maximum length: 256.

backend

string

yes

Backend base URL (http/https) that serves the route.

inject

string

no

Path of the route’s custom injection bundle (JSON), relative to the config file. The bundle declares HTML/JS/CSS insertions by named target ("head" = after <head>/meta charset, "body-end" = before </body>) with per-page targeting (when = path prefix) and data-* attribute patches applied client-side by the guard. Inline content or file: (relative to the bundle, read at load — a faulty bundle refuses startup). Its formal grammar is inject-bundle.schema.json. See the doc’s § upstream.inject.

upstream

object

no

Join to a backend outside the internal network (proxified external site — e.g. Cloudflare Pages/Workers). Absent = unchanged historical behavior: public Host preserved, client headers passed as-is.

frontend

boolean

no

Page route: auth failure → 302 to the login (API routes get a JSON 401); eligible for the guard script and the pwa policy.

autoHead

boolean

no

HEAD requests are served as GET, body removed.

auth

object

no

Authentication policy. Empty ({}) = authentication ALWAYS required. auth.when holds TECHNICAL conditions (method/query/header/body) deciding when authentication is required: one object (AND of its conditions) or an array (OR of ANDs — required if ANY element matches); absent/empty = always required. auth.identity holds IDENTITY conditions (roles/scopes/claims/user), checked after successful authentication (403 otherwise) and only on requests that were actually authenticated.

rateLimit

object

no

Rate limiting: fixed window per identity (authenticated user, else real IP via X-Forwarded-For), per route. Full window = 429 + Retry-After (seconds). Periods: second|minute|hour|day.

quota

object

no

Cumulative quota: same mechanics as rateLimit with a longer window in practice (day). Full window = 429 + Retry-After.

openapi

object

no

OpenAPI document used to derive REST operations and MCP tools for this route.

mcp

object

no

Expose a route as an MCP service: protected-resource identifier, scope, tools and metadata.

pwa

object

no

PWA shell, manifest, icons and service-worker cache policy for a frontend route.

csp

object

no

Content-Security-Policy emitted (or amended) by the gateway — the only component able to generate a per-response nonce and write it into the HTML it already rewrites (guard, PWA, custom injections). By default the origin’s policy is NEVER removed or weakened: the gateway’s policy is added as a SECOND header (browsers enforce all of them, so the effective rule is the strictest) and the hashes of the gateway’s own injected script and guard stylesheet are APPENDED to the origin’s script-src / style-src (script-src-elem > script-src > default-src, style-src-elem > style-src > default-src). Set own=true to remove the origin policy explicitly and let the gateway own it (opt-in, logged, requires mode nonce/hash and reportOnly=false). Applied to HTML responses only.

userBadge

object

no

User badge injected by the guard script once authenticated: collapsed on the top edge (one line = username), expanded on hover/keyboard focus — chosen claims + logout button (OIDC end_session + cookie clearing). Absent = no badge.

uiGate

array of object

no

UI gating by config (CSS selectors) — embedded in the injected guard script. Only for non-modifiable fronts; an element’s data-gtw-* markup wins over the rules.

authGuard

object

no

401 guard script (login without reloading: tab + replay + banner + declarative gating). Active by default on frontend routes; no-op elsewhere. The guard intercepts the 401 (login) and, when authGuard.forbidden.banner is set, the gateway’s OWN identity 403; a 403 coming from the backend is never concerned.

routes.upstream

Join to a backend outside the internal network (proxified external site — e.g. Cloudflare Pages/Workers). Absent = unchanged historical behavior: public Host preserved, client headers passed as-is.

Field Type Required Description

host

boolean

no

true = the Host header sent to the backend is that of the backend’s origin (required for an external site that routes by Host, e.g. Cloudflare — otherwise the request arrives with the public host and the origin does not recognize it). Absent/false = public Host passed as-is (internal backends). TLS/SNI always targets the backend’s origin.

hostOverride

string

no

Explicit value of the Host header sent to the backend, when it must differ from both the public host and the backend’s origin (rare). Precedence over host.

headers

object

no

Static request headers set toward the backend (Set: overwrite any value the client may have sent). Uses: get through an origin basic auth ("Authorization": "Basic ${MYSITE_BASIC_AUTH}") or the Cloudflare Access service tokens (CF-Access-Client-Id / CF-Access-Client-Secret). Values with ${VAR} interpolation from the container environment — missing variable = fatal error at load (never a silent empty credential); empty value = header removed from the request. Values are never logged.

rewriteRedirects
